post.description: Start a charging session using the Auth_id or Chip_id. If the validation is successful the endpoint returns ACCEPTED status as the result. This does not mean that the command was already successfully sent to the charge station yet because of the asynchronous nature of how the OCPP communication works over Websockets. The message id of the OCPP message sent to the charge station will also be returned. This message Id can be used to query the state of the response from the charge station by using the real time status notification API.

### Configure the Network Profile of a Charge Station

Use this command to define the **network connectivity settings** for a charge station. It supports configuring key parameters such as:
- **OCPP version**
- **Transport protocol**
- **CSMS endpoint URL**
- **VPN and APN details**
- Other connection-related options

The configuration is delivered **asynchronously** to the charge station.  
A successful response means the request was **accepted for processing**, but does **not** confirm that the changes have been applied yet.

---

**Warning**
> Changing the OCPP version via the `SetNetworkProfile` command may result in **loss of communication** between the CSMS and the charge station.  
> Upgrades and downgrades are technically supported, but:
> - If you **upgrade** beyond **OCPP 2.0.1**, the charge station will no longer be accessible through the API.
> - If you **downgrade**, you will no longer be able to modify the network profile afterward through the API afterwards.
>  
> **Only OCPP 2.0.1 is officially supported.**  
> It is strongly recommended to keep the version at **2.0.1** unless explicitly instructed by system integrators or support teams.
